subject.title: Gateway auto-injects toolsAllow into isolated agentTurn crons; null patch doesn't clear it; breaks CLI backend

question: How should OpenClaw repair CLI-backed cron jobs that carry flagless `toolsAllow` from the regression window without making explicit per-cron restrictions fail open?
rationale: The availability failure is source-reproducible, but the safe repair depends on maintainer intent for distinguishing stale default caps from intentional restrictions at a runtime tool-policy boundary.

options.title: Add Narrow Stale-Default Repair
options.body: Add a doctor/operator/API repair that marks or clears only provably auto-default regression-window `toolsAllow` values while preserving explicit restrictions as fail-closed.

options.title: Broaden Agent Null Clear
options.body: Allow agent-facing `toolsAllow: null` to bypass creator-surface re-capping, accepting a broader authority change that needs explicit security approval.

options.title: Document Manual Recreate Or Clear
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document that affected jobs must be recreated or repaired through a trusted manual path.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Stale-Default Repair
recommendation.body: Add a doctor/operator/API repair that marks or clears only provably auto-default regression-window `toolsAllow` values while preserving explicit restrictions as fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored the most recent marker-preservation follow-up and is closest to the current edit semantics that decide whether default caps remain marked.
